clues: A capital straddles a tidal river winding east to a wide estuary, on a low plain where chalk hills meet clay in the southeast of a rainy island.
It rains a little all year but rarely pours — the famous 'fogs' were coal smoke, and in past centuries the river froze solid enough for fairs.
Legionaries bridged the river here two thousand years ago; a great tower fortress rose a thousand years later, and a great fire cleared the medieval streets.
Ravens are still kept in its ancient fortress — legend says the kingdom falls if they leave — and its guards wear tall bearskin hats.
Big Ben's tower chimes over the river beside the parliament halls.
